title: Safe Launch Paths — Journey map & fallback micro-interactions
creator: Avery Lin
description: Overview: This ticket contains a consolidated journey map, annotated wireflows, and a set of micro-interaction specs for the Redwood Console's new "safe launch" UX. Objective is to let engineers and product owners configure progressive rollouts (canary, A/B splits) while making worst-case failure modes easy to detect and recover from. This emphasizes explicit fallback controls, low-friction rollback, and clear signals for when automated mitigations should run.
detailed_scope: 1) Journey map: entry points (create rollout, import experiment), in-flight controls (pause, ramp, snapshot), and emergency paths (instant rollback, traffic quarantine). 2) Wireflows: annotated screens for the two primary personas — Platform Operator and Product PM. 3) Micro-interactions: toast and inline confirmations, animated ramp preview, break-glass rollback modal, gradual percentage slider with hysteresis, and keyboard-accessible quick-stop. 4) Observability handoff: inline links to per-variant dashboards and a condensed signal summary panel for each stage.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Use a single canonical traffic slider control to handle both canary and A/B experiments to reduce UI surface area; tradeoff is slightly overloaded control (mitigated with strong affordances and contextual help).
- Provide automated 'safe stop' suggestion based on anomaly detection but default to operator confirmation to avoid unexpected rollbacks.
- Favor explicit, irreversible language on emergency rollback actions with a secondary typed-confirm step only for cross-region rollbacks; local/regional rollbacks use a single confirmation to preserve fast response.
- Avoid heavy animation during high-severity paths to prevent cognitive overload; use simple transitions and status badges instead.
acceptance_criteria: Can create a progressive rollout and configure up to 6 staged ramps with percentage and duration settings
Operator can trigger an emergency rollback that reverts all variants to a baseline in < 10s (UI path validated)
Micro-interactions implemented: confirmation modal, toast error state with "Retry" action, slider hysteresis preventing 1% accidental drifts
Inline link opens the variant's trace dashboard and shows last 10 anomalous requests when available
Accessible via keyboard: ramp slider and emergency rollback modal are fully operable with tab/enter/space and have screen-reader labels
implementation_notes:
- Engineering will receive component spec for the Slider (range, snap points, delay guard) and Rollback modal (typed-confirm for cross-region).
- Provide a JSON schema for the rollout config preview shown in the composer.
- Connect 'suggest safe stop' toggle to Optimize anomaly signals (ENG-78901).
- Performance: keep UI bundle lightweight; defer high-res charts in the popover to server-side prerender if load > 200 active rollouts.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Operators accidentally shift traffic by small amounts. Mitigation: slider hysteresis, keyboard step constraints, and a confirm for changes > 5%.
- Risk: Automated suggestions may cause churn. Mitigation: default off and require explicit opt-in per project with audit log.
- Risk: Rollback latency across regions. Mitigation: staged rollback command that runs primary region first and posts progress updates to UI.
